root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: After `PFETCH(c)` advances the final-byte token, `fetch_token()` must enforce `p <= end` before it publishes `*src = p`.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: The final-byte token must not leave `fetch_token()` with an out-of-bounds token end. The vulnerable original publishes `*src = p` even when `PFETCH(c)` moved `p` past the logical regex end, while the fixed original guards that state with `if (p > end) return ONIGERR_PREMATURE_END_OF_CHAR_CLASS;`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The missing root obligation is the post-`PFETCH` bounds guard on the final-byte token in `fetch_token()`. The required predicate is the source-level relation `p <= end` on the path that continues to `*src = p`.

nodes.description: For the final-byte token, `fetch_token()` publishes `*src` as an end pointer that already exceeds the logical regex `end`.
`node_new_str()` receives the same out-of-bounds token end as its `end` argument when `parse_exp()` materializes the final token span.
At the sanitizer sink, `onig_node_str_cat()` receives an `end` pointer past the logical regex end, so its copy span crosses the payload boundary.

edges.description: The post-`PFETCH` cursor `p` is published unchanged as `*src` for the final token.
`parse_exp()` forwards the published `*src` pointer unchanged into `node_new_str(..., end)` for the same final token span.
`node_new_str()` passes the same out-of-bounds `end` argument straight into `onig_node_str_cat(node, s, end)`.
